solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Draw out its shock when announcing an award (8,5)

indicatorNotes.when announcing: announcing means saying it out loud, so the phrase is heard rather than read

blocks.note: draw out = pull, shock = surprise: say "pull its surprise" quickly

annotation.surface: Someone teasing out the drama when a prize winner is read out.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads like advice on building suspense at a ceremony, but the phrase "pull its surprise" is simply said out loud.
annotation.definitionFit: The Pulitzer Prize is an American award for journalism, literature and music.

entries.clue: Tasty drink turning up on a list (9)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, turning a word up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to lap is to drink, as a cat does
a table is a list, as in a league table

annotation.surface: A nice drink that shows up on a menu.
annotation.walkthrough: "Drink" looks like a noun on a drinks list; it is the verb lap, which turns up to PAL.
annotation.definitionFit: Palatable food or drink is pleasant to taste.

entries.clue: Unusually creditable and moral politician (7,8)

indicatorNotes.Unusually: the letters are set out in an unusual order

annotation.surface: A rare thing: a politician who is honest and decent.
annotation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a UK political party; the clue's joke is that a creditable, moral politician is unusual.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a member of a UK centrist party is one kind of politician.

entries.clue: Shoots without opening negotiations (5)

indicatorNotes.without opening: the word loses its opening, its first letter

blocks.note: STALKS (plant shoots) loses its first letter S

annotation.surface: A gunman firing before any talks have begun.
annotation.walkthrough: "Shoots" suggests gunfire, and "opening negotiations" suggests a phrase; the break falls after "opening".
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: diplomats' formal discussions, as between warring sides, are called both.

entries.clue: Worrying about rent, busted for begging (10)

indicatorNotes.about: EATING goes about, around, the other piece
indicatorNotes.busted: a busted thing is broken, so RENT's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: eating = worrying, as in "what's eating you?"

annotation.surface: A broke tenant, anxious about the rent, reduced to pleading.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface paints a broke tenant, but "busted" is not money trouble: it tells you to break up the word beside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean pleading earnestly with someone for something.

entries.clue: French not accepting width in feet (4)

indicatorNotes.accepting: to accept something is to take it in, so PAS takes W inside itself

annotation.surface: A Frenchman who refuses to measure anything in feet.
annotation.walkthrough: "in feet" looks like part of the measuring picture; it links the wordplay to the definition, feet.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym for animals: a cat's or dog's feet have their own name.

entries.clue: Like clumsy words he refined with Collins (3-6)

indicatorNotes.refined: refining reworks material, so the letters are reworked

annotation.surface: A writer polishing his clumsy prose with the help of a Collins dictionary.
annotation.walkthrough: Collins is a well-known dictionary publisher, which fits the picture of fixing clumsy words; here it is just seven letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive phrase: words that land clumsily were badly picked for the moment.

entries.clue: Dancing tutor got behind a military show (9,6)

indicatorNotes.Dancing: dancing letters move about into a new order

annotation.surface: A dance teacher falling behind the troops in a parade.
annotation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Military Tattoo is an annual display of military bands on the esplanade of Edinburgh Castle in Scotland.
annotation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a military display with bands, and Edinburgh's is the most famous.

entries.clue: Like French toast for one chap on vacation (4)

indicatorNotes.on vacation: a vacated word has been emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

blocks.note: GUY (chap) emptied of its middle U

annotation.surface: A man away on holiday eating French toast for breakfast.
annotation.walkthrough: "On vacation" sounds like a holiday; in crosswords it means the word is emptied.
annotation.definitionFit: French toast is bread soaked in beaten egg and fried, so it is eggy.

entries.clue: Mark Lambert, murder victim (5)

blocks.note: the lambert is an old unit of brightness, symbol L
Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

annotation.surface: A news report naming Mark Lambert as a murder victim.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mark Lambert" reads as a man's full name; Mark is the definition and Lambert only gives its unit symbol L.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tag or brand stuck on something, noun or verb alike.

entries.clue: Soft material, effective protecting old whisky (9)

indicatorNotes.protecting: TELLING wraps around the other letters to protect them

blocks.note: a telling blow is an effective one
Whisky is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A soft cloth that does a good job of wrapping a bottle of old whisky.
annotation.walkthrough: "Old whisky" suggests a vintage malt; it is two single letters, O and W, placed inside TELLING.
annotation.definitionFit: Towelling is the soft looped fabric that towels are made of.

entries.clue: Party leading newsman to get hammered (8)

blocks.note: a thrash is a lively party

indicatorNotes.leading: THRASH goes in front of, leading, ED

annotation.surface: A party where the lead journalist ends up very drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: In the surface "hammered" means drunk; the definition is the other sense, soundly beaten.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang synonym: both mean soundly beaten, though the surface wants hammered's drunken sense.

entries.clue: Old man on cold stout (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one piece placed on another is attached after it, so HUBBY follows C

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
one's old man is one's husband, informally hubby

annotation.surface: An elderly man drinking cold stout.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stout" looks like the dark beer; it is the adjective meaning plump.
annotation.definitionFit: Chubby and stout both mean plump.

entries.clue: Explosive coverage of The Sunday Times competition (10)

indicatorNotes.coverage of: TNT covers, goes around, the other piece

blocks.note: printed in The Sunday Times, the paper's title is "our name"

annotation.surface: A newspaper's sensational reporting of its own contest.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter speaks as the newspaper, so The Sunday Times is OUR NAME.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a contest run over a series of rounds, as in tennis or chess.

entries.clue: A mechanical part in an inventor’s trousers (4-7)

indicatorNotes.in: the mechanical is literally in the inventor's name, so BOTTOM sits inside BELLS

blocks.note: Alexander Graham Bell invented the telephone: "Bell's"
Bottom, the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, is a part played by one of the "rude mechanicals"

annotation.surface: A machine component caught in an inventor's trousers.
annotation.walkthrough: "Mechanical part" suggests a cog; Shakespeare's mechanicals are the amateur tradesmen-actors of the Dream, and Bottom is the best known.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the flared-leg style of trousers popular in the 1970s.

entries.clue: Order about a month before a dance (5,4)

indicatorNotes.before: A NOV comes before, above, the final A

blocks.note: to boss about is to order about
a + NOV, the abbreviation for November

annotation.surface: Choreographing a month of rehearsal ahead of a dance.
annotation.walkthrough: NOV is the calendar abbreviation for November; "about" is part of the phrase "order about", not a container.
annotation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance to samba-jazz music.

entries.clue: Odd page ripped from behind (3)

indicatorNotes.ripped from: P is torn away from the word

annotation.surface: A strange page torn out of the back of a book.
annotation.walkthrough: "From behind" reads as "from the back"; behind is the noun, RUMP. Rum is British slang for odd.
annotation.definitionFit: Rum is an old British word for odd or peculiar.

entries.clue: Crazy write-up, mostly on Eastern coral (9)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, all but its last letter
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, REPOR sits on top of E

annotation.surface: A wild article written about corals in the East.
annotation.walkthrough: Madrepore is an uncommon word, so build it from the pieces: MAD, most of REPORT, then E.
annotation.definitionFit: Madrepore is a reef-building stony coral.

entries.clue: Second in the race, out of seven (3)

indicatorNotes.out of: the answer is taken out of the next word

blocks.note: the three letters inside, with the S and N stripped off

annotation.surface: A runner finishing second in a field of seven.
annotation.walkthrough: "The race" is the human race: in Genesis Adam came first and Eve second.
annotation.definitionFit: Eve was the second human created, after Adam.

entries.clue: Enclosure with hundreds working outside bathed in light (3-8)

indicatorNotes.working: the letters are worked into a new order
indicatorNotes.outside: the rearranged letters sit outside ENC

blocks.note: enc. is the abbreviation for an enclosure in a letter

annotation.surface: A field pen with hundreds of labourers toiling out in the sunshine.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hundreds" looks like C or CC; it is the word itself, rearranged, and it wraps ENC.
annotation.definitionFit: Sun-drenched means flooded with sunlight.

entries.clue: Fastener husband used to secure a pipe (6)

indicatorNotes.used to secure: HOOK H goes around A, holding it in place

annotation.surface: A husband using a clip to hold a pipe in place.
annotation.walkthrough: "a pipe" reads as one phrase, but the "a" is what HOOK H secures; the definition is "pipe" alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the water pipe that draws smoke through a bowl of water.

entries.clue: Barrier set low in response to crack? (2-2)

blocks.note: a garden wall sunk in a ditch so it does not spoil the view
a crack is a joke, and the response is laughter

annotation.surface: A low barrier put up after a crack appears in a wall.
annotation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a sunken fence found in English country-house gardens; the question mark flags "crack" as a joke, not a split.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a landscape gardener's sunken fence, and the laughter a wisecrack earns.

entries.clue: Salt measure added to pastry (8)

indicatorNotes.added to: RATE is added to the end of TART

blocks.note: a rate is a measure, as in speed

annotation.surface: A pinch of salt added to pastry dough.
annotation.walkthrough: The baking picture hides a chemistry definition: salt as a chemical compound.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a chemical salt of tartaric acid, as in cream of tartar.

entries.clue: Tip on triangular sword’s conical housing (5)

indicatorNotes.Tip: the tip of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, T sits on top of EPEE

blocks.note: an épée is a fencing sword

annotation.surface: The point of a three-sided blade and the cone-shaped sheath it sits in.
annotation.walkthrough: "Conical housing" sounds like a scabbard for the sword; it is a tent.
annotation.definitionFit: A tepee is a cone-shaped tent of the Plains peoples of North America.

entries.clue: A French filmmaker’s worn out broadcast (4)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: something broadcast is heard, so the word goes by its sound

annotation.surface: A French director's shabby old film shown on television.
annotation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati made comic films such as Monsieur Hulot's Holiday; the "'s" is "is", joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was a French filmmaker and comic actor.

entries.clue: Spa hotel or a great alternative (9)

indicatorNotes.alternative: an alternative arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Choosing between a spa hotel and some other great place to stay.
annotation.walkthrough: Harrogate is a spa town in Yorkshire, in the north of England.
annotation.definitionFit: Harrogate grew famous for its mineral springs, so it is a spa.

entries.clue: Vegetable left by a primate (5)

indicatorNotes.left by: the vegetable is left, abandoned, by A

annotation.surface: A monkey leaving behind a vegetable.
annotation.walkthrough: "Left by a primate" reads as one phrase; "a" belongs to the wordplay and "primate" alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The potto is a small slow-moving primate of African forests.

entries.clue: Food hopper where a chip might go? (4-2-3-4)

blocks.note: in golf, a chip shot might go in the hole

annotation.surface: A food container, and the question of where a stray chip ends up.
annotation.walkthrough: Toad-in-the-hole is a British dish of sausages baked in batter; the chip is a short golf shot, not a French fry.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a British dish of sausages baked in batter is one kind of food.
